passage: Asif dragged a chair to the kitchen cupboard, where the jar of sweets sat on the top shelf. He climbed up, stretched, and found he was still too short. He fetched the stool and lifted it onto the chair. His older brother Santosh walked in at that moment. "Stop. Don't climb that, it will tip." Santosh held the chair still and called, "Papa! Asif wants the jar." Papa took the jar down and gave each of them one sweet.

qa.q: What did Asif drag to the cupboard first?
qa.a: Asif dragged a chair to the cupboard first.

qa.q: What was Asif feeling when he found he was still too short on the chair?
qa.a: Asif was frustrated but still determined, because he wanted the sweets. He fetched the stool to try again.

qa.q: What safer approach could work, and why?
qa.a: Asif could have called an adult to lift the jar down. A grown-up is tall enough, and a stack of chair and stool could tip.

qa.q: How does the tower look to Santosh?
qa.a: Santosh sees a dangerous stack and a fall waiting to happen. Stopping Asif and calling Papa keeps everyone safe.

grounding: A child tries a chair, then adds a stool, to reach the sweets, and an older brother stops the climb and calls for help.

passage:
"Darshan, what are you doing?" Rehana, his big sister, stood in the kitchen doorway.
"Getting sweets." He hauled a chair over to the cupboard and climbed on it. His fingers stretched. "Too short!"
He jumped down, fetched the little stool and started lifting it onto the chair.
"Stop! That's not safe!" Rehana ran over, lifted him down and held him. "You could fall. I'll get the jar."

qa.q: What did Darshan haul over to the cupboard?
What was Darshan feeling when he said "Too short!"?
qa.a: He was frustrated but still determined to reach the sweets.

qa.q: What would you change first in Darshan's plan?
qa.a: Ask a grown-up or his sister for the jar, because stacking a stool on a chair can make him fall.

qa.q: How does the stacking look to Rehana?
qa.a: Rehana is scared and worried he'll fall, so she stops him and helps.

grounding: A child drags a chair to reach a jar, finds it too short and starts to add a stool, and his sister stops him and helps.

passage:
Note for Minakshi's parents, from the babysitter
This afternoon Minakshi pulled a chair to the kitchen cupboard to get the sweets jar. She stood on the chair; still too short. Then she began to lift the small stool onto the chair. I came in at that moment, took the stool away, held her hand and helped her down. I explained why stacking is dangerous. She was upset. I gave her one sweet and put the jar lower.

qa.q: What did Minakshi try to lift onto the chair?
What was Minakshi feeling when the babysitter took the stool away?
qa.a: She was upset and disappointed not to get the sweets herself.

qa.q: What else could the family do to keep Minakshi safe?
qa.a: Keep treats where she can ask easily, and remind her to call a grown-up for high things.

qa.q: How might Minakshi's parents feel reading the note?
qa.a: They would likely feel alarmed at the stacking and relieved it was stopped straight away.

grounding: A babysitter's note describes a child who stands on a chair, finds it too short and starts adding a stool, and is stopped before climbing.
